title: Universal protocol for the wafer-scale manufacturing of 2D carbon-based transducer layers
author: Lu, Munief, et al.

steps.title: Physical Plasma Surface Activation
steps.instruction: Place the wafer (Au, glass or silicon) in the plasma stripper, evacuate to vacuum and run an O₂ plasma at 40 % O₂, 50 W for 30 s; then wait 10 min before silanization, or if activation and silanization are performed without venting, wait 30 min under vacuum to allow oxygen radicals to decay.

steps.title: Chemical Cleaning and Activation
steps.instruction: Immerse silicon wafers in Caro’s acid (H₂SO₄ 98 wt % : H₂O₂ 30 wt % mixed 1:3) at 120 °C for 20 min; rinse thoroughly with de‑ionized water; dry with a N₂ stream for 1 min; spin‑rinse‑dry at 1700 rpm for 3 min then 2000 rpm for 4 min; perform a quick‑dump rinse (same spin speeds and times) before proceeding.

steps.title: Gas‑Phase Silanization of Substrate
steps.instruction: Introduce silane vapor into the reactor after the activation step: use aminothiophenol (ATP) for Au substrates (thiol binds Au) or (3‑aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) for glass or silicon (silane binds surface hydroxyls). Allow sufficient exposure time as recommended by the silane supplier (not specified in the source).

steps.title: Spin‑Coat GO Dispersion
steps.instruction: Pipette approximately 6 mL of GO aqueous dispersion (pH = 2.1) onto the silane‑modified wafer until the surface is fully covered; immediately spin at 3500 rpm with no ramp until the film is formed.

steps.title: Post‑Spin Bake for Amide Formation
steps.instruction: Place the GO‑coated wafer on a hot plate at 150 °C for sufficient time (typically 5–10 min) to complete condensation of silane amino groups with GO carboxyl groups, forming amide bonds across the entire 4‑inch surface.

steps.title: Photolithography for Conductive Tracks (Mask 1)
steps.instruction: Pattern Ti/Au conductor tracks using the following sequence:

substeps.instruction: Spin‑coat image‑reversal photoresist AR‑U 4030: dispense 3 mL, spin 7 s at 100 rpm, then 60 s at 3000 rpm (target thickness 1.7 µm).
Soft‑bake on hot plate at 85 °C for 2 min; rest 10 min.
Expose through mask type 1 using mask aligner: 10 s, 6 mW, hard‑contact mode.
Post‑exposure bake at 115 °C for 5 min; rest 10 min.
Flood expose (hard‑contact) for 25 s at 6 mW.
Reverse develop with AR 300‑26 developer diluted DI 1:3 for ~10 s.
Spin‑rinse‑dry: 2700 rpm for 3 min then 2000 rpm for 4 min.
Inspect pattern with optical microscope and film‑thickness probe (FTP).

steps.title: Photolithography and RIE Patterning of GO (Mask 3)
steps.instruction: Define GO micro‑/nano‑structures on the wafer:

substeps.instruction: Spin‑coat positive photoresist AR‑U 4030 using the same parameters as above (3 mL, 7 s @100 rpm, 60 s @3000 rpm).
Soft‑bake 85 °C for 2 min; rest 10 min.
Expose through mask type 3: 10 s, 6 mW, hard‑contact.
Post‑exposure bake 115 °C for 5 min; rest 10 min.
Flood expose 25 s, 6 mW.
Reverse develop with AR 300‑26 (DI 1:3) ~10 s.
Spin‑rinse‑dry 2700 rpm 3 min, 2000 rpm 4 min.
Inspect with microscope and FTP.
Reactive‑ion etch (RIE) in O₂ plasma: reactor pressure 15 Pa, O₂ flow 4.8 sccm, RF power 100 W, etch time 20 s.
Inspect etched pattern with microscope and FTP.

steps.title: Photoresist Removal after RIE
steps.instruction: Clean the wafer by immersing in acetone for 5 min followed by isopropanol for 5 min; then dry with N₂.

steps.title: Metal Deposition of Ti/Au Electrodes
steps.instruction: Deposit Ti/Au conductive tracks onto the patterned wafer using electron‑beam evaporation (or equivalent) under high vacuum; thicknesses as required for the device (not specified).

steps.title: Borosilicate Glass Passivation (BSK)
steps.instruction: Hermetically seal the Ti/Au tracks with a borosilicate glass (BSK) layer of 200 nm thickness by appropriate glass‑fusing or sputtering technique, ensuring coverage of the entire conductor area for operation in high‑ionic‑strength solutions.

steps.title: Nanoimprint Lithography of GO (Mask 4)
steps.instruction: Create sub‑100 nm GO nanoribbons using NIL:

substeps.instruction: Spin‑coat nanoimprint resist (PMMA, mr‑I 7020R) filtered through 0.22 µm syringe: dispense 2–3 mL, spin 30 s at 1000 rpm, then 60 s at 3000 rpm (target thickness 200 nm ± 15 nm).
Soft‑bake on hot plate at 100 °C for 1 min; rest 10 min.
Perform NIL with silicon master stamp: Step 1 – pressure 40 bar, T = 115 °C, t = 300 s; Step 2 – T = 115 °C, pressure 1 bar, t = 5 s.
Inspect imprint depth (≈200 nm) with microscope/FTP.
Remove residual layer and pattern GO by O₂‑RIE: pressure 13.3 Pa, O₂ flow 3.1 sccm, RF power 100 W, etch time 35 s.
Final inspection of GO nanoribbons (lengths 45 µm or 4 µm, width 150 nm, thickness 1–3 nm).

steps.title: Residual Layer Removal and GO Nanoribbon Etch
steps.instruction: After NIL, perform an O₂‑RIE step to strip the residual PMMA layer and to etch the exposed GO, using the parameters listed in the previous step (13.3 Pa, 3.1 sccm O₂, 100 W, 35 s). Verify dimensions with SEM.
